T: The party that saves the branch.
D: A branch manager throws an epic office Christmas party to save his staff from being sacked.
P: Serve the snacks when the party gets out of hand.
S: Golden sausage rolls with tomato sauce, the first thing to disappear off any office party table.
Brie, cheddar, crackers and grapes on a big board, the classy part of the night before things get messy.
M: the catering at the out-of-control party
Little beef sliders with cheese and pickles, the kind of party food you can eat with one hand.
W: Vanilla cupcakes with red and green buttercream, the Christmas colours the office goes all in on.
K: Chilled eggnog with nutmeg, rum on the side for the adults.

s.how: Mix 500g sausage mince with 1 grated onion and roll in 2 sheets puff pastry. Brush with milk, cut into short lengths and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with tomato sauce.
Arrange 150g brie and 150g cheddar on a big board with 200g crackers and 500g grapes. Let the cheese come to room temperature for 30 minutes before the party starts.

m.note: the catering at the out-of-control party
m.how: Shape 500g beef mince into 12 small patties and season well. Cook on a hot grill for 2 minutes a side, add cheese to melt and serve in 12 slider buns with pickles and sauce.

w.how: Beat 125g butter and 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, 200g self-raising flour and 120ml milk. Bake 12 cupcakes at 180C for 18 minutes. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar, tint half red and half green and pipe on.

d.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g sugar. Pour in 800ml hot milk and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon. Chill well and serve with grated nutmeg and rum on the side.
